rationale: The study examines post-independence agricultural land reform, privatization of former state and collective farms, and elite capture of farm organizations (FOs) and agricultural water user associations (WUAs) by collective farm managers and farm hydro-technicians in Uzbekistan. Because it concerns agricultural production and farm irrigation management rather than household or community domestic water or sanitation service access, it clearly fails Criterion 1 (exclusion code E07).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings because the study fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 (E07: agricultural land reform, farm organizations, and agricultural irrigation water user associations rather than household or community water or sanitation service access).

evidence_quotes.quote: Uzbek farm organizations (FOs) & water user associations (WUAs) were & are supposed to be democratic & participatory -- & therefore an enabling factor for privatization, local water management, & agricultural production

During the first reform only parts of the land of former state & collective farms were privatized. In the second reform these farms were abolished, their land privatized, & local water management was decentralized.

The paper reveals how the collective farm managers not only secured agricultural land, but also how they together with the hydro-technicians hold on to their power positions through the establishment of FOs & WUAs.
